problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{4}{3s+6}.$
worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t}} & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{s+2}=\frac{4}{3s+6},\,s>-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t}} & =\frac{4}{3s+6} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{3s+6}} \\ \frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{3s+6}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{3s+6}} & =\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$
